content: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim, marketed as Bactrim, should be used judiciously to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of this and other antibacterial agents. These medications should only be prescribed for the treatment or prevention of infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria susceptible to these drugs. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform empirical therapy choices. Urinary Tract Infections (UTIs): Bactrim is indicated for the treatment of urinary tract infections caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli, Klebsiella species, Enterobacter species, Morganella morganii, Proteus mirabilis, and Proteus vulgaris. For initial episodes of uncomplicated UTIs, it is recommended to use a single effective antibacterial agent rather than a combination therapy. Acute Otitis Media: Bactrim is indicated for the treatment of acute otitis media in pediatric patients when caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae. This is recommended only when the physician determines that sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim provide a distinct advantage over other antimicrobial agents. However, there is limited safety data on the repeated use of Bactrim in pediatric patients under two years of age. Additionally, Bactrim is not recommended for prophylactic or prolonged use in otitis media at any age. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis in Adults: Bactrim may be used to treat acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis caused by susceptible strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae or Haemophilus influenzae. This is appropriate when the physician believes that Bactrim offers an advantage over the use of a single antimicrobial agent. Shigellosis: Bactrim is indicated for the treatment of enteritis caused by susceptible strains of Shigella flexneri and Shigella sonnei when antibacterial therapy is deemed necessary. Pneumocystis jiroveci Pneumonia (PJP): Bactrim is used for the treatment of documented Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia. It is also indicated for prophylaxis against P. jiroveci pneumonia in immunosuppressed individuals who are at increased risk of developing this infection. Traveler’s Diarrhea in Adults: Bactrim is indicated for the treatment of traveler’s diarrhea caused by susceptible strains of enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli.
